Authorities are cited only to the indexed library (`library/INDEX.md` — `faa_2_4.md`, `fee_shifting_and_candor.md`, `columbia_account_stated_waiver.md`, `columbia_tortious_interference.md`); anything outside it is labeled **unverified**.
14:**Their opening offer is not close, and we should say so plainly.** The Halvorsen posture recorded October 20 offers the four conceded invoices at **$265,200 — principal only, no interest — paid over six months**, with **zero** on J-4533, **zero** conversion fees, a mutual release, and each side bearing its own fees. Measured against our own arithmetic:
16:- It is **$12,720.27 below** even the conceded block at the filing basis (277,920.27 − 265,200.00) — i.e., it buys the released settlement by waiving every dollar of interest they have already conceded they owe.
21:**The flag (prominently, and built on nothing):** that note is dated **October 20** — five days *before* our October 25 demand and twenty-two days after their September 29 letter. It does not say who took the call, which side they were on, or who wrote it, and it reached this office's files only with the Session 5 materials. Its *substance* matches Pinecrest's own written positions of September 29, so we use its substance — but its **provenance is unexplained**, and I have asked you exactly one new question about it (Q11: who participated, what was actually said about interest and the payment schedule, and any fuller note). Until answered, every figure below is used on the note's face and labeled — nothing here forces the strict and generous readings to reconcile.
23:**The instrument in one breath:** concede-block paid unconditionally at the filing basis ($277,920.27, interest stops at receipt); J-4533R paid with a shift-level audit true-up ($74,161.70 at the filing basis; our $3,100 credit stands); conversion fees paid at the $80,000* estimate with a true-up to 25% of documented actual compensation; mutual release with each side bearing its own fees; the forward §3 undertaking; live through November 10, otherwise we file on November 11. Never below $309,920.27 without your informed, on-the-record election.
35:- Daily interest while unpaid: **$112.30/day** ($88.40 conceded four + $23.90 J-4533R), from 336,900 × 1%/30. **Every payment stops §2 interest at receipt.**
45:| **Floor** | the conceded four, whatever else happens | **$277,920.27** |
53:| **Generous** — if "the four undisputed invoices" were shorthand including accrued interest to signing | 265,200 + 11,217.47 | **$276,417.47** |
55:Gaps against our verified lines, on the strict reading: −12,720.27 vs. the filing-basis floor (277,920.27 − 265,200.00); −44,720.27 vs. the walk-away (309,920.27 − 265,200.00); −166,881.97 vs. the filing projection (432,081.97 − 265,200.00). Even the most generous reading still sits **$33,502.80 below the walk-away** (309,920.27 − 276,417.47), and it zeroes $154,161.70 of claim value (J-4533R 74,161.70 + conversions 80,000) while stretching the rest six months. **Under every reading it fails the walk-away. That is bad news delivered plainly: their number is below the money their own lawyer has conceded in writing.**
65:**T-2 Conceded invoices — unconditional.** The four invoices (J-4411, J-4452, J-4490, J-4571) are payable at principal **plus §2 interest accrued through the date of payment**, wired within five business days of execution. Working figure at the November 11 filing basis: **$277,920.27** (October 25 anchor $276,417.47; payment earlier lowers the figure by $88.40 per day earlier — §2 stops interest at receipt). **This payment obligation is independent of every true-up below** — the decoupling we put in writing on October 27 is preserved inside the instrument: the conceded money is never held hostage to any dispute. If Pinecrest can only close on installments, §2 continues at 1%/month on unpaid balances (the $9,282 benchmark in §2.3), and that offset must be priced into the deal, not waived by silence.
67:**T-3 J-4533R — payable, with a shift-level true-up.** Payable at principal $71,700 plus §2 interest from the original due date through receipt (**$74,161.70** at the filing basis). Pinecrest may produce documented, shift-level findings for any hours it claims were not worked; documented findings adjust the principal on that shift, moving the total up or down — the same standard both ways. Whatever the true-up yields, the $3,100 double-entry credit we already gave in J-4533R **stands**. If Pinecrest's position is $0 (their October 20 words), then their September 29 Point 3 standard — notice given within 15 days, hours "padded" — must be shown, not asserted: their own letter concedes they "reviewed the parties' agreement in full," and the 15-day dispute window had run when we issued the invoice.
86:- **Both gives together = $309,920.27 — the walk-away (Scenario D).** Below that, filing dominates on this record: their lawyer has conceded the core in writing twice (September 29 letter; October 20 call), and even losing both fights still nets $309,920.27 with §2 interest accruing until receipt.
98:- **For your board narrative, this instrument is the same story you already have:** the admitted money is the strong part — now confirmed twice in Pinecrest's own words (their September 29 letter; the October 20 posture offering to pay those four at all); the headline is smaller than at Session 1 because of **our own $3,188.87 correction**, not theirs; the realistic number is ≈ **$430,172.87** on the October 25 basis and $432,081.97 at the filing projection; the $862,000 was never supported, and we have never claimed otherwise; and the fee clause cuts both ways — their October 20 words prove it in their own voice.
-------
**Recommendation:** reject as stated, hold the November 11 arbitration filing, counter only at or above the walk-away (§3–§4). What the posture is useful for: it confirms both fights will be run exactly as the Session 4 memo predicted (J-4533 and the conversion fees all to $0), it reconfirms in their own words that the fee clause cuts both ways, and it gives us one already-aligned term: **mutual release, each side bears its own fees** — which is what we were going to propose anyway (§3, T-6).
